summary.text: Jay Feely is a former NFL placekicker (2001-2014) and CBS football analyst, and the Republican nominee for Arizona's 1st Congressional District, an open seat. He played college football at the University of Michigan and began his congressional campaign in 2025, first in the 5th District and later in the 1st. As of July 1, 2026, he had raised $2.53 million to Amish Shah's $1.83 million.

paragraphs.text: Born May 23, 1976, and attended Jesuit High School in Tampa, Florida, according to Wikipedia.
Earned a bachelor's degree in finance from the University of Michigan in 1998, where he was a four-year letterman as a kicker.
Began his professional career with the Florida Bobcats (1999) and Tampa Bay Storm (2000) of the Arena Football League.

Played as a kicker for six NFL teams from 2001 to 2014, including the Atlanta Falcons, New York Giants, Miami Dolphins, New York Jets, Arizona Cardinals (2010-2013), and Chicago Bears. He was named to the Pro Football Weekly All-Rookie team in 2001.
After retiring, joined CBS in 2015 as a college football analyst for CBS Sports Network and later worked as an NFL analyst and color commentator for CBS.
Announced in April 2025 that he would run as a Republican in Arizona's 5th District, then announced on December 19, 2025 that he would run in the 1st District instead.
Won the July 21, 2026 Republican primary with 49.8% of the vote over Joseph Chaplik (35.7%) and John Trobough (14.5%); Wikipedia reports he was endorsed by President Donald Trump.
Lives in Gilbert, Arizona, with his wife, Rebecca; the couple have four children, according to Wikipedia. His campaign website cites his charitable work in the community.
